lead: The neighbourhood that lives in the shadow of Gaudí's temple, with local shops and a strong neighbourhood spirit.
text: Until not long ago it was called "el Poblet": for years it was mostly countryside, with a small cluster of low houses around Carrer de València, and it had no identity of its own until the early 20th century, when it became a working-class neighbourhood beside many factories. The temple was planned in 1881, on land in the Sant Martí district where everything around was fields, and it has been growing at its centre since 1882; Gaudí, then young and little known, took over when the crypt was being started.

From its façade runs Avinguda de Gaudí, which leads on foot to the Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau by Domènech i Montaner, and both buildings are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. On the streets beside the temple you share the pavement with visitors from all over the world, but a few blocks away life is that of a neighbourhood of neighbours, with a market, shops and schools. With 53,201 inhabitants in 1.04 km², it is one of the most densely populated in the Eixample, and its average rent, 1,107 €/month, is the lowest in the district.
housing: Flats in buildings of the Cerdà grid, with more visitor traffic beside the temple.
